clue.text: Rock room, turning away leader of criminals

indicators.note: turning signals that the abbreviations for rock and room are read in reverse

parts.note: GIB is the short name for Gibraltar, known as the Rock

explanation.surface: A rock band's room is moving away from the head of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning away' reverses GIB + RM. Gibraltar is widely nicknamed the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock nickname for the boss of a criminal gang, used in thrillers and the press.

clue.text: Timid hangman trembles, needing utmost strength

indicators.note: trembling shakes the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous executioner shakes, needing every ounce of power to do his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembles' shuffles TIMID HANGMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'with all one's force' uses this phrase to mean maximum effort and power.

clue.text: Bishop forces sports fans abroad

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
forces in the plural is read as two armies, one after the other

explanation.surface: A bishop forces supporters overseas into line.
explanation.walkthrough: B + ARMY makes the first word, and a second ARMY follows: 'forces' gives two of them. The answer is the nickname of the travelling supporters of England's cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for England cricket supporters who follow the team on overseas tours.

clue.text: Hard work is great in service? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the clue's order is reversed, so the service goes inside great rather than the other way round

parts.note: GT is a standard abbreviation of great, as in Gt Britain
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Is doing hard labour a fine thing when serving others? No, quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'great in service' would put the great word inside; 'On the contrary' tells you to swap which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal synonym for toil or sustained labour.

clue.text: Together in firm, the lower classes fawned around one

definitions.note: the words 'in' and 'firm' run together make 'infirm', meaning frail

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification system

indicators.note: around has the fawning word enclose the letter for one

parts.note: crept means behaved obsequiously
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A company where the lower ranks grovel around somebody, all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together' tells you to join 'in' and 'firm' into one word for the definition. The British social grades run A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so the lowest two classes are D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone weak and worn out through age or illness.

clue.text: "Democrat in, Tories out!" — that is to confuse

indicators.note: out signals the following letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An election slogan: Democrats in power, Conservatives gone, which would bewilder everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the slogan, ousting the Tories, but it is the signal to rearrange 'in Tories'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone off their bearings so they lose track of where they are, a near synonym for bewilder.

clue.text: Start to cut, shape and grind

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to hew is to shape by cutting, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Instructions in a workshop: begin cutting, form the piece, then sand it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Working food with the teeth crushes it, a sense of grind.

clue.text: Old king's service perhaps about to save the pound

indicators.note: saving keeps the phrase about the pound safe inside
about turns the tree word round

parts.note: the service tree is a European tree of the rose family, so service is one example of a tree
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's royal service seems to be about rescuing the currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks service as one kind of tree (the service tree), not a church or royal service. 'about' turns the tree round to EERT before it wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Anglo-Saxon rulers bore the name, notably a king of Kent around 600.

clue.text: I fight to seize Republican ground

indicators.note: seizing means the fight word grips the letter for Republican

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A boxer vows to wrestle a Republican to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to seize' puts R inside BOX. The answer is the football stadium of Rangers in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A football ground: the Glasgow home stadium of Rangers FC.

clue.text: One may help police drag men off, keeping peace at first between two women

indicators.note: keeping means the shuffled letters hold the next part inside them
off says the letters of these words are thrown into a new arrangement
between places the letter between the two words for women

parts.note: SHE and HER are two pronouns for women, standing side by side

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A police dog drags men away while a pair of women keep the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DRAG MEN into GERMAND, which then splits to hold the women and P; 'two women' are the pronouns for a woman, not names.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is the classic police dog, used by forces to track and restrain suspects.

clue.text: To be clear, on planets not our own there is no opening for life

indicators.note: there is no means the letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: planets other than ours are other worlds, so on them is in other worlds

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scientist clarifies that alien planets cannot begin to support living things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there is no' removes L ('opening for' life) from IN OTHER WORLDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used to restate something more plainly, which serves to clarify.

clue.text: Flirts with right-winger, getting one animated

parts.note: someone who toys with another flirts with them
a Tory is a member of the right-wing UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with a conservative politician and gets excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' looks like excited; here it means a cartoon film. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1995 Pixar feature was the first fully computer-generated cartoon film.

clue.text: Racists bearing cross round as warning

indicators.note: bearing means carrying the following letters within

parts.note: the Klan is a notorious American white-supremacist organisation
X is the shape of a cross
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Extremists carrying a cross in procession serve as an alarm signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' puts X and O inside KLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud electric horn, originally a trade name, used to sound an alarm.

clue.text: What Piaf had indoors at intervals — waders

indicators.note: taking letters at intervals picks every other one

parts.note: egrets are long-legged wading birds of the heron family

explanation.surface: The French singer kept fishing boots inside the house, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes the even letters of INDOORS: N, O, R. Piaf's famous song declares she regrets nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf's signature song 'Non, je ne regrette rien' says she regretted nothing.

clue.text: Being possible to reach, successfully phone restaurant

definitions.meaning: describes something accessible or within reach
ringing a restaurant and securing a reservation for a meal

explanation.surface: Being reachable means you can book a dinner by phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the hyphenated adjective as a three-word phrase about booking.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for attainable or accessible, built from the verb phrase meaning obtain.

clue.text: Hear master had a seizure, having overindulged

indicators.note: hear says the following phrase is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: sir is a word for master, and fitted means had a fit or seizure

explanation.surface: Word goes round that the boss collapsed in a fit after eating too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' asks for the sound of SIR FITTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be glutted means having had too much of something, especially food.

clue.text: Take part of sheet (the bottom) and stick back

indicators.note: back reverses the word for stick

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut off the bottom of a sheet of paper and glue it on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CANE; 'the bottom' of sheet is T.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a role on stage is to act out a part.

clue.text: Purple with fresh air and bungee jumping

indicators.note: jumping sets the letters of the two words bouncing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone turns purple with the fresh air of a bungee jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' shuffles AIR and BUNGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark purple of the eggplant's skin gives its name to the colour.

clue.text: Tucking into acorns? At first you are allowed to

indicators.note: tucking into puts the first letter inside the word for acorns

parts.note: mast is the fallen fruit of forest trees such as acorns and beechnuts

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: Eating acorns? Initially, you have permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, but places Y ('At first' of you) inside MAST. The answer is the old form used with thou.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic second-person form of may, as in 'thou mayest', expressing permission.

clue.text: Record holder's go on board

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A player's move in a board game is recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating platform of a record player holds a vinyl disc.

clue.text: Two or three prepositions, altogether

definitions.meaning: the letters can be split into two prepositions (...) or three (...)

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson counting prepositions, all in all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase can be split as INTO + TO or IN + TO + TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means entirely, completely, in all respects.

clue.text: Tennis's beginning on grass in a moment

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Tennis matches on grass start in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: Rice belongs to the grass family, so 'grass' gives RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short time, as in the phrase 'in a jiffy'.

clue.text: Strong feelings leading to hard argument — over its expansion?

definitions.text: Strong feelings leading to hard argument — over its expansion?

parts.note: heat means intense passion or anger
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Passions run high in a fierce dispute about enlarging something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the long dispute over a third runway at London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: London's largest airport has been the subject of a fierce, long-running dispute over a new runway.

clue.text: Murdered, throat cut — get the law!

indicators.note: murdered signals that the letters are mangled into a new order
cut removes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crime scene: a victim with a slit throat, so call the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last T of THROAT, and 'Murdered' shuffles THROA. 'get the law' looks like calling the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish law, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Inspiration taken from heraldic lion

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An artist draws ideas from a lion on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' extracts the letters in heraldiC LIOn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of history in Greek myth; a muse is a source of creative inspiration.

clue.text: Dangerous creature in trap? Rubbish — fright that is for nothing

parts.note: a pit is a trap for animals
bull is slang for nonsense

indicators.note: for means one thing is swapped in place of another

parts.note: terror is great fright
O looks like zero, nothing
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something deadly in a trap? Nonsense, that fear is groundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts IE in place of the O in TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighting dog breed with a reputation for aggression, banned in the UK.

clue.text: I say Anna is a cow

parts.note: an exclamation calling attention, like 'here!'
Anna Ford is a well-known British television newsreader

explanation.surface: An insult: somebody calls Anna an unpleasant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like an insult but means the cattle breed. Anna Ford read the news on BBC and ITN.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of red-and-white beef cattle from the English county of the same name.

clue.text: Gardeners stand nervously around spades? Not very

indicators.note: not means the letter for very is left out

parts.note: to hover is to linger anxiously nearby
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Gardeners hang about anxiously near the spades, though not too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes V (very) from HOVER + S.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work soil with a hoe, a weeding tool, are gardeners by example.
